Ecosystems are connected by flows of matter and organisms: what one ecosystem
exports shapes the recipient one. This is idea of @Loreau-Mouquet-Holt-2003,
@Gounand-etal-2018a]. Rivers deliver to estuaries and coastal waters the
nutrients, sediment and freshwater released by their catchment. Here, we ask how
the land use and climate of the catchment shape the fish communities of
estuaries and coastal bays, in the four districts of interest.

Here are our hypotheses of driver impacts on estuarine and coastal ecosystems.

**Hypotheses.** Fish are grouped by their use of estuaries (guilds, see
below).

| Driver | Expected change | Expected effect on the communities |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Farmland (arable) | More nitrate and phosphate exported; more fine sediment and turbidity | Moderate enrichment raises the productivity of nurseries: more marine juveniles (flatfish, sea bass); strong enrichment brings algal blooms and hypoxia: fewer sensitive estuarine residents and marine juveniles |
| Urban areas | More ammonium, organic matter and contaminants | Fewer marine juveniles and sensitive residents, more tolerant species |
| Rainfall of the year, catchment size | More freshwater: lower salinity, more nutrients delivered | More freshwater and diadromous species, fewer marine stragglers; higher nursery production of sole in wet years |
| Temperature (catchment and year) | Warmer water; with nutrients, more hypoxia | More warm-water marine species and residents, fewer cold-water species (plaice, whiting, smelt, flounder) |

Steps: (1) data and guilds, (2) the catchment of the estuary of each
operation, (3) models of the communities (to come).


## Setup

```{r setup}
library(renv)
renv::load()
library(targets)
library(here)
tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets")
)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
devtools::load_all()
nice_theme()
```

```{r palette}
guild_label <- c(
  MS = "Marine straggler", MM = "Marine migrant (juveniles)", ER = "Estuarine resident",
  CA = "Diadromous", FW = "Freshwater"
)
colour_guild <- c(
  `Marine straggler` = "#56B4E9", `Marine migrant (juveniles)` = "#0072B2",
  `Estuarine resident` = "#009E73", Diadromous = "#E69F00", Freshwater = "#CC79A7"
)
colour_effect <- c(Positive = "#2166AC", `Not credible` = "grey70", Negative = "#B2182B")
survey_label <- c(pomet = "POMET (estuaries)", nurse = "Nursery survey (coastal bays)")
colour_survey <- c(`POMET (estuaries)` = "#D55E00", `Nursery survey (coastal bays)` = "#0072B2")
```

## Data

Two trawling survey surveys: POMET and nursery survey (NURSE).

We keep the operations of the four districts, at sea and inland (upper
estuaries), with their distance to the river mouth (D8; target
`sea_operation`). Each operation is then linked to a river mouth (see
[Catchment of each estuary](#catchment-of-each-estuary)).

Salinity is measured at most POMET operations; for the nursery survey and
the other POMET operations, it is taken from the yearly modeled environment
of the Bay of Biscay coast.

```{r data}
operation <- tar_read(sea_operation)
catch <- tar_read(sea_catch)
operation |>
  summarise(
    Operations = n(),
    Years = paste(min(year), max(year), sep = "-"),
    Months = paste(sort(unique(month)), collapse = ", "),
    `Salinity measured` = scales::percent(mean(salinity_source == "measured", na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `Salinity from the grid` = scales::percent(mean(salinity_source == "grid", na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `No salinity` = sum(is.na(salinity)),
    .by = c(survey, gear)
  ) |>
  mutate(survey = survey_label[survey]) |>
  rename(Survey = survey, Gear = gear) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r map}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Operations of the two surveys in the four districts."

france <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", country = "France", returnclass = "sf")
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = france, fill = "grey95", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(
    aes(longitude, latitude, color = survey_label[survey]),
    data = operation, size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = range(operation$longitude) + c(-0.3, 0.3), ylim = range(operation$latitude) + c(-0.3, 0.3)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colour_survey) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.line = element_blank())
```

### Species and guilds

Each species is classed by its use of estuaries, from the guilds of the
POMET reference (target `estuary_guild`), matched on the names validated
against FishBase (the reference uses older names, e.g. *Liza ramada* for
*Chelon ramada*), completed by hand for the species missing from it and
corrected by hand for a few (target `species_guild`, notes in the table
below).

The five guilds are the estuarine-use functional groups of
@Elliott-Quintino-2007.

| Guild | Description | Examples |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Marine straggler | Marine species spawning at sea that enter estuaries occasionally and in low numbers, mostly near the mouth; they do not depend on estuaries. | dragonet, solenette, red mullet, weevers |
| Marine migrant (juveniles) | Marine species spawning at sea whose juveniles enter estuaries and shallow bays in large numbers to grow (nurseries), before returning to sea; adults may also feed there seasonally. | sole, sea bass, plaice, whiting, sprat, thick-lipped and golden grey mullets |
| Estuarine resident | Species completing their whole life cycle in the estuary (and shallow coastal waters). | gobies, pipefishes, sea horses |
| Diadromous | Species migrating between the sea and fresh water to complete their life cycle, through the estuary: anadromous ones spawn in rivers (shads, smelt), catadromous ones spawn at sea (eel, flounder, thin-lipped grey mullet). | eel, flounder, smelt, shads |
| Freshwater | Freshwater species entering the upper, low-salinity part of the estuary. | roach, bream, pikeperch |

```{r guild}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Number of species of each guild and share of the occurrences (species x operation), per survey."

catch |>
  inner_join(select(operation, operation_id, survey), by = "operation_id") |>
  mutate(guild = coalesce(guild_label[guild], "Unclassified")) |>
  summarise(species = n_distinct(species), occurrences = n(), .by = c(survey, guild)) |>
  mutate(share = occurrences / sum(occurrences), .by = survey) |>
  mutate(
    survey = survey_label[survey],
    guild = factor(guild, c(names(colour_guild), "Unclassified"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(share, survey, fill = guild)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = species), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3, color = "white"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(colour_guild, Unclassified = "grey70")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Share of the occurrences (numbers: species)", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

```{r guild-table}
species_guild <- tar_read(species_guild)
catch |>
  inner_join(select(operation, operation_id, survey), by = "operation_id") |>
  count(species, survey) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  inner_join(species_guild, by = "species") |>
  mutate(guild = factor(guild_label[guild], guild_label)) |>
  arrange(guild, desc(pomet + nurse)) |>
  transmute(
    Species = paste0("*", species, "*"), Guild = guild,
    `POMET operations` = pomet, `Nursery survey operations` = nurse,
    `Guild source` = source, Note = coalesce(note, "")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```


## Catchment of each estuary

Each operation is linked to the main river flowing into its estuary or
bay, and related to the land use of that river's catchment. Small streams
entering the same estuary (e.g. the marsh channels along the Gironde) are
merged with its main river: the water of the estuary comes mostly from
it.

- **Main rivers:** the AMOBIO river mouths (as in D8) draining 1,000 km²
  or more; mouths closer than 3 km are pooled (e.g. the Orne and the Dan
  at Caen).
- **Catchments:** computed on the HydroSHEDS flow directions (~400 m, as
  in D15). Each grid outlet takes the main river its stream reaches along
  the AMOBIO network: e.g. the Garonne and the Dordogne, which end at the
  head of the Gironde on the grid. Land cover and weather are read from
  the cached catchment rasters of D15.
- **Operations:** inland (upper estuaries), the main river reached along
  the network; at sea, the nearest main river mouth along the sea (D8),
  if within 15 km. The other operations are dropped. By hand: the
  operations of the Gironde estuary belong to the Gironde (the AMOBIO
  Gironde ends at its head, 20 to 70 km from them).

Targets: `main_mouth`, `network_mouth`, `mouth_outlet`,
`sea_operation_mouth`, `mouth_catchment`.

```{r mouth}
mouth <- tar_read(sea_mouth_area)
basin <- tar_read(mouth_basin)
operation_mouth <- operation |>
  select(operation_id, survey, district, longitude, latitude) |>
  left_join(tar_read(sea_operation_mouth), by = "operation_id")
mouth_used <- mouth |>
  filter(mouth_id %in% operation_mouth$mouth_id) |>
  arrange(district, desc(latitude))
palette_mouth <- c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#CC79A7", "#8C6D31")
colour_mouth <- setNames(rep_len(palette_mouth, nrow(mouth_used)), mouth_used$mouth_id)
```

```{r mouth-catchment}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Catchments of the main rivers with operations (one colour per river), and the operations kept (black) or dropped (grey, more than 15 km from a main river mouth at sea)."

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = france, fill = "grey95", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = factor(mouth_id)), data = filter(basin, mouth_id %in% mouth_used$mouth_id), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude), data = filter(operation_mouth, is.na(mouth_id)), size = 0.2, color = "grey55") +
  geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude), data = filter(operation_mouth, !is.na(mouth_id)), size = 0.2) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    aes(longitude, latitude, label = river), data = mouth_used,
    size = 2.6, label.size = 0.1, label.padding = 0.15, min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = 0.2, seed = 1
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-5.2, 6), ylim = c(43, 51.2)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colour_mouth, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

```{r mouth-operation}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 13
#| fig-cap: "Operations coloured by their main river (triangle: mouth), per district; grey: dropped."

map_district <- \(d) {
  op <- filter(operation_mouth, district == d)
  m <- filter(mouth_used, mouth_id %in% op$mouth_id)
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = france, fill = "grey95", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude), data = filter(op, is.na(mouth_id)), size = 0.4, color = "grey70") +
    geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude, color = factor(mouth_id)), data = filter(op, !is.na(mouth_id)), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(longitude, latitude, color = factor(mouth_id)), data = m, shape = 17, size = 2.4) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      aes(longitude, latitude, label = river, color = factor(mouth_id)), data = m,
      size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", bg.color = "white", bg.r = 0.15,
      min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = 0.2, max.overlaps = Inf, seed = 1
    ) +
    coord_sf(xlim = range(op$longitude) + c(-0.1, 0.1), ylim = range(op$latitude) + c(-0.1, 0.1)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colour_mouth, guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = d) +
    theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = 7))
}
row_north <- patchwork::wrap_plots(map_district("Escaut-Somme"), map_district("Seine"), widths = c(1, 2.5))
row_south <- patchwork::wrap_plots(map_district("Loire"), map_district("Ardour-Garonne"), widths = c(2, 1))
patchwork::wrap_plots(row_north, row_south, ncol = 1, heights = c(1, 2))
```

```{r mouth-table}
operation_mouth |>
  filter(!is.na(mouth_id)) |>
  count(mouth_id, survey) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = survey, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  inner_join(mouth, by = "mouth_id") |>
  arrange(desc(area)) |>
  transmute(
    River = river, District = district, `POMET operations` = pomet,
    `Nursery survey operations` = nurse, `Catchment (km²)` = round(area)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

**Results:**

- `r nrow(mouth_used)` main rivers, from about 1,000 km² (Laïta, Rance)
  to 118,000 km² (Loire), with the large rivers at their known size
  (Gironde 82,000 km², Seine 76,000, Vilaine 10,500).
- `r format(sum(!is.na(operation_mouth$mouth_id)), big.mark = ",")` of
  `r format(nrow(operation_mouth), big.mark = ",")` operations are kept:
  most POMET operations (estuaries) but few nursery survey operations
  (bays away from the main mouths).

*To discuss:*

- Land use varies only between the `r nrow(mouth_used)` rivers, so its
  effects rest on few units.
- The bays dropped here could be added back with a land use exposure
  summing the main rivers nearby, weighted by distance at sea.
